clue.text: Carpenter, for one, producing a flier

definitions.meaning: in Lewis Carroll's poem the Walrus and the Carpenter lure and eat a bed of oysters, so the Carpenter is a catcher of them
a flier is anything that flies, here a black-and-white wading bird

explanation.surface: Some carpenter turns out a printed leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a leaflet; it is a bird. The Carpenter is the one from 'The Walrus and the Carpenter' in Alice Through the Looking-Glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a shoreline wader named for prising shellfish open, and the Carpenter literally gathers shellfish in Carroll's poem.

clue.text: Amass too many weapons for normal method of delivery in the field

definitions.meaning: to equip with more armaments than needed

definitions.text: normal method of delivery in the field
definitions.meaning: in cricket, bowling with the arm swung above the shoulder

explanation.surface: An army stockpiling guns for how it usually fights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery in the field' is cricket: bowling, which must be done with the arm above the shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive arming is one sense, and the standard cricket bowling action with the arm high is the other.

clue.text: Winning measure from brusque person in charge

parts.note: brusque means curt or short in manner
a head is a leader or chief

explanation.surface: A curt manager decides the margin of victory.
explanation.walkthrough: In horse racing a short head is the narrowest winning margin, less than a horse's head.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing, the smallest margin by which a horse can be judged to have won.

clue.text: Listening device covering most of the ground

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the next, covering it

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing

indicators.note: most of says the final letter of the word the is dropped

explanation.surface: A bugging device placed to cover most of the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' places EAR above TH (the without its last letter) in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Soil or land is synonymous with the dirt beneath one's feet.

clue.text: Friar's broken china cup

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: broken says the letters of china and cup are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A monk has smashed a china cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friar's' reads as possessive; it is 'Friar is'. 'Broken' scrambles CHINA CUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a Franciscan order known for their pointed hoods, also giving the monkey its name.

clue.text: Rower's bench made from block

definitions.meaning: the crosswise seat in a rowing boat
to block is to frustrate or foil

explanation.surface: A rowing seat carved from a block of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat across a boat for an oarsman, and as a verb to obstruct or frustrate plans.

clue.text: Difficult to fill with food and liquor

parts.note: hard means difficult
to stuff is to cram with food

explanation.surface: It is hard to fill up with food and drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquor' seems to be part of a list with food; it is the definition, slang for strong spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for strong spirits such as whisky, as opposed to beer or wine.

clue.text: Love at first sight admitted by one who regrets being king

indicators.note: admitted by says the letter is let inside the other piece

parts.note: a ruer is someone who rues, or regrets

indicators.note: at first sight picks the opening letter of the word love

explanation.surface: A monarch regrets love at first sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love at first sight' is a set phrase; here 'at first sight' only takes L from 'Love', which goes into RUER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign such as a monarch governs a land.

clue.text: Backslider in the Cabinet, perhaps?

parts.note: a backslider sounds like a minister who lapses, but it is something that slides back into a cabinet of furniture

explanation.walkthrough: The Cabinet suggests government ministers; it is a chest of furniture, with a part that slides back in.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliding box in a chest or cabinet that pulls out and pushes back in.

clue.text: Excursion on which one pleases oneself?

definitions.text: Excursion on which one pleases oneself?

parts.words: Excursion on which one pleases oneself?
parts.note: read literally, a trip taken purely for the self, the inner I; really an act of vanity indulging one's own importance

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the 'excursion' is figurative: a self-indulgent exercise in vanity rather than a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A vain, self-indulgent venture is described as a journey made for the gratification of one's own self-image.

clue.text: Sort of fly with rook or another bird

parts.note: the warble fly is a fly whose larvae burrow under cattle hide
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: An angler chooses between a particular fly and a rook as bait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' looks like a bird beside 'another bird', but it is the chess piece, abbreviated R.
explanation.definitionFit: A songbird of the Old World family Sylviidae, named for its trilling song.

clue.text: Small island church coming to its end

definitions.note: the end of the word church is the letter H, and the definition names that letter as spelt out

parts.note: an ait (or eyot) is a small island in a river, especially the Thames

explanation.surface: A tiny island chapel is finally closing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its end' points back at 'church': the last letter of that word is H, whose spelt-out name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The final letter of the word church is H, and this is how the name of that letter is written in full.

clue.text: Opener in county's team

parts.note: Cork is a county in Ireland; with the possessive it gives CORKS
a crew is a team, as of rowers

explanation.surface: A cricket opening batsman plays for his county side.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an opening batsman in a county cricket team; the 'opener' is the tool for drawing corks from bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral tool for pulling stoppers from wine bottles is a kind of bottle opener.

clue.text: Verse, perhaps, that gives one something to remember

definitions.text: Verse, perhaps, that gives one something to remember

parts.words: Verse, perhaps, that gives one something to remember
parts.note: a rhyme or jingle whose job is to help a person recall facts, like 'Thirty days hath September'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that verse is only one example; any memory aid, rhymed or not, fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A memory aid such as a rhyme or acronym is designed to help someone recall information.

clue.text: Unwell, having bad complexion

definitions.meaning: literally having a skin tone that is wrong or poor

explanation.surface: Feeling ill, with a pasty face.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase for feeling slightly ill, and literally a poor or wrong hue.

clue.text: Unusually large and troublesome delivery

definitions.meaning: a ... crop or harvest is an exceptionally big one
in cricket, a short ball that rears up at the batsman's head

explanation.surface: An outsized and difficult childbirth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' suggests childbirth, but it is a cricket ball bowled so it bounces high at the batsman, also called a bouncer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes an abundant crop or issue, and in cricket a short-pitched rising ball.

clue.text: Strange interplay in a shared service

indicators.note: strange says the letters of interplay are rearranged into an odd order

explanation.surface: Odd interplay arises in a joint arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' scrambles INTERPLAY. A party line is also a telephone line shared by several subscribers.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone line shared by several subscribers is a communal phone connection.

clue.text: Title of his play composed about daughter

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go round the abbreviation
composed says the letters of his play are rearranged

explanation.surface: The name of his play is written about his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' scrambles HIS PLAY into LAYSHIP; 'about' wraps that round D.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of address used for a woman of noble rank, such as a peeress.

clue.text: Revise, poem by unknown at Scottish festival

parts.note: a Mod is a Gaelic festival of music and poetry held in Scotland
If is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns, like x and z

explanation.surface: A poet amends an anonymous verse entered at a Highland festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poem' wants a general word like ODE; here it is the specific Kipling poem 'If'. 'Unknown' is an algebra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise something is to alter or adjust it, a synonym.

clue.text: Mouse taken to guy

definitions.meaning: the cartoon mouse created by Walt Disney
to take the ... is to tease or guy someone

explanation.surface: A mouse is carried to a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is the verb meaning to mock; the mickey is what is taken when someone is teased.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's cartoon rodent shares the name, and taking the mickey means mocking.

clue.text: Flourishes ticket money for football followers

indicators.note: ticket money for followers reads as fares belonging to fans, so the fans' word stands in front

parts.note: a fan is a supporter of a football team
fares are the money paid for travel tickets

explanation.surface: Ticket prices rise for travelling football supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as 'fan fares', fares for fans, which joins into the trumpet calls of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanfares are flourishes of trumpets, short ceremonial calls announcing someone.

clue.text: Deceptive movement brings vehicle in on time

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on the next

parts.note: a sleigh is a vehicle on runners

explanation.surface: A deceptive movement brings the car in on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: SLEIGH sits 'on' T in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is skilful trickery, a deceptive move.

clue.text: Fuse has explosive in the middle

indicators.note: in says the explosive piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the core is the centre of something
HE is high explosive

explanation.surface: A bomb's fuse has explosive in its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuse' looks like part of a bomb; it is the verb, to join together.
explanation.definitionFit: To fuse is to join or stick together into one.

clue.text: How one deals with foot-faults in service

definitions.text: How one deals with foot-faults in service

parts.words: How one deals with foot-faults in service
parts.note: a tennis foot fault at service suggests sport, but the faults are ailments of the feet treated professionally

explanation.walkthrough: Tennis players commit foot faults when serving; here the 'foot-faults' are corns and bunions, and 'service' is a professional health service.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical treatment of feet and their ailments is a professional service.

clue.text: "Hippy" found in Brazilia cadging

indicators.note: found in says the answer is concealed inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A hippie is seen begging in Brazil's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hippy' looks like a flower-child; it means relating to the hip.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to the hip region, as in the bone.

clue.text: Manner of performing steps, say

indicators.note: say marks that the word for steps is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a fence or wall

explanation.surface: How a dancer performs steps, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' suggests dancing, but it is the countryside stile over a fence, which sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's distinctive way or fashion of doing something is their manner.

clue.text: Wise man of old cut short farewell

indicators.note: cut short says the word for farewell loses its final letter

parts.note: so long is a farewell

explanation.surface: An ancient sage cut short his goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: Solon was an Athenian statesman and lawgiver, a byword for wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian statesman was famed for his wisdom, so his name means a sage.

clue.text: Typical example of back exercises one found heavy work

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation for exercises is read in reverse

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
I is the Roman numeral for one
a tome is a large, heavy book

explanation.surface: Back exercises are someone's idea of a perfect heavy workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back exercises' reads as exercises for the back; 'back' turns PE into EP.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect example embodying the type is its very essence, the quintessence.

clue.text: Serving a portion of food

definitions.meaning: assisting or aiding, as in lending a hand
a single serving put on a plate

explanation.surface: A waiter dishes up a plate of food.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means giving aid as well as a single measure dished out at a meal.

clue.text: Journalist runs into person cited in court case

indicators.note: into says the abbreviation for runs goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a co-respondent is the third party named in a divorce case as the lover
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A reporter bumps into someone named in a divorce case.
explanation.walkthrough: A co-respondent is the person accused of adultery in a divorce petition; add R for runs to get a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper reporter covering a particular subject or place, such as a foreign news writer.
